hints: Look carefully at where the dark chromosomes are in each photo, lined up in the middle, pulled apart, arrived at the ends, or already in two separate cells.
Remember the order of mitosis is metaphase, then anaphase, then telophase, then cytokinesis, so ask which photo shows chromosomes already at opposite poles.
walkthrough:
**Observe the chromosome positions**

Look at each cell. In A they line the middle. In B they are in V-shapes moving apart. In C they are in two tight groups at opposite ends. In D there are two round nuclei in two separate cells.

That visual pattern is your biggest clue.

**Recall the order of mitosis**

Mitosis runs in order: prophase, then metaphase (chromosomes on equator), then anaphase (sister chromatids pulled apart), then telophase (two sets arrive at poles and start to decondense).

Cytokinesis, splitting of the cytoplasm, comes after telophase.

**Choose the last stage before cytokinesis**

A is metaphase and B is anaphase, so both are too early. D already shows two daughter cells after cytokinesis.

C shows telophase, with two chromosome groups at the poles just before the cell divides, so it is the last stage before cytokinesis.

options.A: Shows metaphase, with chromosomes lined up on the metaphase plate, which is two stages before cytokinesis.
options.B: Shows anaphase, with sister chromatids separating toward poles, which is one stage before telophase and cytokinesis.
options.C: Shows telophase, with two sets of chromosomes at opposite poles, which is the final stage of nuclear division just before cytokinesis.
options.D: Shows after cytokinesis, with two separate daughter cells each with its own nucleus, so it is too late.
